The `literal` argument is also discarded. Execution returns successfully, making the wrong-handler behavior easy to miss.\n\nThe same command tree behaves correctly with `TraverseChildren: false`.\n\n## Environment\n\n- Cobra commit: `adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e`\n- pflag: `v1.0.9`\n- OS/architecture: Linux/amd64\n- Go: `go1.27.2-X:nodwarf5`\n\n## Minimal reproduction\n\nSave as `main.go` in an empty directory:\n\n```go\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t"fmt"\n\t"os"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\troot := &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse:              "app",\n\t\tTraverseChildren: true,\n\t\tArgs:             cobra.ArbitraryArgs,\n\t\tRun: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Printf("root called with %q\\n", args)\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\troot.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse: "child",\n\t\tRun: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Println("child called")\n\t\t},\n\t})\n\tif err := root.Execute(); err != nil {\n\t\tos.Exit(1)\n\t}\n}\n```\n\nInitialize and build:\n\n```sh\ngo mod init example.com/cobra-traverse-repro\ngo get github.com/spf13/cobra@adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e\ngo build -o app .\n```\n\nRun:\n\n```sh\n./app -- literal child\n```\n\n## Actual behavior\n\n```text\nchild called\n```\n\nThe child handler runs, `literal` is discarded, and the process exits with status 0.\n\n## Expected behavior\n\n```text\nroot called with ["literal" "child"]\n```\n\nThe delimiter should stop command discovery on this path, consistent with the default `Find` path. Both subsequent tokens should remain positional arguments for the root command.\n\n## Controls\n\nChange only `TraverseChildren: true` to `TraverseChildren: false`, rebuild, and rerun the same command. It produces the expected root output.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`:\n\n```sh\n./app -- child\n# root called with ["child"]\n\n./app -- literal other\n# root called with ["literal" "other"]\n\n./app child\n# child called\n```\n\nThese controls show that the failure depends on the later positional token matching an existing subcommand after the first post-delimiter token has been consumed.\n\n## Cause\n\nIn [`Command.Traverse`](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e/command.go#L821-L857), the long-flag branch also matches a bare `--`:\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--") && !strings.Contains(arg, "="):\n    inFlag = !hasNoOptDefVal(arg[2:], c.Flags())\n    flags = append(flags, arg)\n    continue\n```\n\nFor `--`, `arg[2:]` is empty, so no flag is found and `inFlag` becomes true. The next token (`literal`) is consumed as a supposed flag value. `Traverse` then resumes command discovery, finds `child`, parses the accumulated `["--", "literal"]` on the parent, and recurses into the child with the remaining arguments. The parent\'s positional arguments are not passed to that child.\n\nThe default `stripFlags` path explicitly stops discovery on `--`, whereas this traversal path does not.\n\n## Impact and additional verification\n\nApplications using `TraverseChildren` can run an unintended command handler when positional data after `--` matches a child command name. Arguments before that match may also be lost.\n\nThe reproduction uses a fresh process and requires neither user-defined flags nor completion setup. Three repeated regression runs reproduced the failure with `TraverseChildren: true`, while the otherwise identical `false` control passed each time.\n\nUpstream `main` was checked on 2026-10-15. Its `command.go` had the same blob SHA as the tested local file: `c05fed45aef0cfed0304728c2289aa18fb152dad`.\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'aditya-rai-5'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-10-15T18:15:51Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-15T18:15:51Z'}, {'number': 2527, 'title': 'Shell completion parses flags twice, duplicating array/slice values and doubling count flags', 'body': '## Description\n\nA single `__complete` request parses the target command\'s flags twice before calling its completion callback. As a result, repeatable flag values differ between normal execution and completion:\n\n- `StringArrayVar`: one `--tag one` becomes `["one", "one"]`.\n- `StringSliceVar`: the same duplication occurs.\n- `CountVarP`: one `-v` produces `2` rather than `1`.\n\nThis occurs with a fresh command in a fresh process. It does not require repeated calls to `Execute`, and reproduces without installing or sourcing a shell completion script.\n\n## Environment\n\n- Cobra commit: `adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e`\n- pflag: `v1.0.9`\n- OS/architecture: Linux/amd64\n- Go: `go1.27.2-X:nodwarf5`\n\n## Minimal reproduction\n\nSave this as `main.go` in an empty directory:\n\n```go\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t"fmt"\n\t"os"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\tvar tags []string\n\tvar verbose int\n\tstate := func() string {\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf("tags=%q verbose=%d", tags, verbose)\n\t}\n\tcmd := &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse: "app",\n\t\tRun: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Println(state())\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tcmd.Flags().StringArrayVar(&tags, "tag", nil, "tag")\n\tcmd.Flags().CountVarP(&verbose, "verbose", "v", "verbosity")\n\tcmd.ValidArgsFunction = func(*cobra.Command, []string, string) ([]cobra.Completion, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {\n\t\treturn []cobra.Completion{state()}, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp\n\t}\n\tif err := cmd.Execute(); err != nil {\n\t\tos.Exit(1)\n\t}\n}\n```\n\nInitialize the module and build:\n\n```sh\ngo mod init example.com/cobra-completion-repro\ngo get github.com/spf13/cobra@adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e\ngo build -o app .\n```\n\nRun normal execution as a control:\n\n```sh\n./app --tag one -v\n```\n\nOutput:\n\n```text\ntags=["one"] verbose=1\n```\n\nNow run completion in a separate process:\n\n```sh\n./app __complete --tag one -v \'\'\n```\n\nActual stdout:\n\n```text\ntags=["one" "one"] verbose=2\n:4\n```\n\nStderr also contains the normal `Completion ended with directive: ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp` message. The final empty argument represents the next word being completed after a space.\n\n## Expected behavior\n\nThe completion callback should observe the same flag values as normal execution:\n\n```text\ntags=["one"] verbose=1\n:4\n```\n\nEach user-supplied flag occurrence should apply once during this request.\n\n## Impact\n\nCompletion callbacks receive incorrect input when they depend on previously supplied array, slice, or count flags. This can produce incorrect filtering, selection, or verbosity during completion. The reproduction demonstrates incorrect state inside the completion process; it does not show persistent corruption of a separate normal command execution.\n\n## Cause\n\nIn [`getCompletions`](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e/completions.go#L367-L383), the same live flag set is parsed twice:\n\n```go\n_ = finalCmd.ParseFlags(append(finalArgs, "--"))\nnewArgCount := finalCmd.Flags().NArg()\n\nif err = finalCmd.ParseFlags(finalArgs); err != nil {\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nThe first parse probes whether flag completion should stop after `--` or a positional argument with interspersed parsing disabled. However, it also changes real flag values. The second parse then appends/increments them again. Scalar flags may hide this because assigning the same value twice gives the same result.\n\nA fix should preserve delimiter/interspersed handling without applying stateful flag setters twice.\n\n## Additional verification\n\n- Both `__complete` and `__completeNoDesc` reproduce the problem.\n- `--tag one --tag two -vv` yields tags `["one", "two", "one", "two"]` and count `4` during completion.\n- Confirmed with argument completion (`ValidArgsFunction`) and registered flag-value completion (`RegisterFlagCompletionFunc`), on root commands and subcommands.\n- Array, slice, and count regression cases were run three times; normal-execution controls passed each time and completion cases failed each time.\n- The upstream `main` version of `completions.go` was checked on 2026-10-15 and had the same blob SHA as the tested file: `9a8259fe7e912dbf10b269a673a6141df96ac344`.\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'aditya-rai-5'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-10-15T18:02:20Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-15T18:02:20Z'}, {'number': 2525, 'title': '"passthrough" arguments and flags?', 'body': 'I\'m new to Cobra (and Viper and other related stuff). There\'s a small part of what I\'m hoping to use it for that\'s not really _necessary_, but it would be nice, and I\'ve thus far been unable to find info on how to accomplish it cleanly and not-extremely-verbosely. First, a little general background:\n\nThere\'s a third-party CLI app (let\'s call it `third`) that supports all sorts of complicated behavior, but that I only actually use in a pretty limited way. I\'d like to use Cobra to make a CLI app (let\'s call it `wrap`) that will act as a wrapper for invocations of `third`, simplified for my personal usage.\n\nThe most simple possible invocation of `wrap` would be:\n\n> wrap wrap-cmd required-arg-1 required-arg-2\n\nDepending on what exactly `wrap-cmd` is, that will wind up invoking something that might be like:\n\n> third third-cmd required-arg-1 required-arg2 --some-third-flag --some-other-third-flag arg-for-some-other-third-flag\n\nSo that seems easy enough to do with Cobra. I\'d also like to allow optional flags for `wrap` itself and for the various possible `wrap-cmd` commands. Both such things would affect exactly how `third` is invoked. These also seem easy enough to with Cobra. But next comes the part I\'m not so sure about:\n\nI\'d furthermore like to support optional flags and arguments for `third` itself (mostly just so I can keep using `wrap` even in some weird little edge case that I haven\'t really specifically considered yet). So, what I\'d really like here is something like:\n\n> wrap wrap-cmd required-arg-1 required-arg-2 --some-wacky-third-flag\n\nWhich would translate to:\n\n> third third-cmd required-arg-1 required-arg2 --some-third-flag --some-other-third-flag arg-for-some-other-third-flag --some-wacky-third-flag\n\nObviously this _can_ be done, but the only ways I\'ve thought of have been either not terribly clean, for example...\n\n> wrap wrap-cmd --wrap-cmd-flag-saying-the-next-thing-is-a-flag-for-third --some-wacky-third-flag required-arg-1 required-arg-2\n\n... or else extremely verbose, explicitly telling Cobra about every one of the bazillion possible `third` options.\n\nIs there a way to do this sort of thing in a way that is both clean and also _not_ extremely verbose? For example, syntax like the "what I\'d really like here" shown above, where Cobra would consider everything (if anything) specified past `required-arg-2` to just be general things that should be accepted no matter what they look like?\n\nThanks in advance for any help.', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'rwv37'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 1, 'created_at': '2026-10-11T04:25:39Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-13T03:25:52Z'}, {'number': 2520, 'title': 'Generated man pages put flag and description on one line', 'body': 'Man pages from `doc.GenMan` / `GenManTree` print each flag\'s description on the same line as the flag. Long descriptions wrap back to the left margin. From restic\'s `restic-backup.1`, generated by `restic generate --man` (`MANWIDTH=80`):\n\n```\n     -n, --dry-run[=false]      do not upload or write any data, just show what\n     would be done\n\n     -e, --exclude=[]      exclude a pattern (can be specified multiple times)\n\n     --exclude-caches[=false]      excludes cache directories that  are  marked\n     with  a  CACHEDIR.TAG file. See https://bford.info/cachedir/ for the Cache\n     Directory Tagging Standard\n```\n\nExpected is the usual tagged-paragraph layout:\n\n```\n     -n, --dry-run[=false]\n            do not upload or write any data, just show what would be done\n\n     -e, --exclude=[]\n            exclude a pattern (can be specified multiple times)\n\n     --exclude-caches[=false]\n            excludes cache directories that  are  marked  with  a  CACHEDIR.TAG\n            file. See https://bford.info/cachedir/ for the Cache Directory Tag‐\n            ging Standard\n```\n\nThis is a regression from cobra v0.0.6, which moved to go-md2man v2 (#977). `manPrintFlags` writes the usage on a tab-indented line after the flag. go-md2man v1 kept that line separate, v2 joins it with the flag into one paragraph. @MichaelEischer reported it in [#1049](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1049#issuecomment-708654517), but that issue was closed with the `.TH` fix.\n\nTo reproduce:\n\n```go\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t"os"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra/doc"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\tcmd := &cobra.Command{Use: "demo", Short: "Demo command", Run: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {}}\n\tcmd.Flags().String("name", "", "Name of the thing")\n\tcmd.Flags().StringP("output-directory", "o", "", "Directory to write the generated files to, created if it does not exist yet")\n\t_ = doc.GenMan(cmd, nil, os.Stdout)\n}\n```\n\n```\ngo run . > demo.1 && man -l demo.1\n```\n\nWith cobra v0.0.5 each description is on its own line. With v0.0.6 up to v1.10.2 it is on the option line, the gap after each option differs, and the long one wraps back to the margin.\n\nI generated the man pages of docker, hugo, restic, caddy and helm with their own commands, and all of them have this layout. gh fixed it in its own copy of the generator by writing the usage as a go-md2man definition list ([cli/cli#4939](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/4939)), which renders as `.TP`.\n\nI have a fix with a regression test and will open a PR.\n\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'seflue'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-10-05T20:08:23Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-05T21:41:29Z'}, {'number': 2507, 'title': 'Eq panics for two individually supported operand types', 'body': '### Description\n\nThe exported template helper `Eq` documents that it supports `int` and `string` values and that unsupported types panic. Its implementation dispatches only on the first operand, then calls the corresponding reflection accessor on the second operand. Two individually supported values of different kinds therefore panic instead of returning `false` or producing a clear same-kind precondition error.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n```go\npackage main\n\nimport "github.com/spf13/cobra"\n\nfunc main() {\n    _ = cobra.Eq(1, "1")\n}\n```\n\nThe first operand selects the signed-integer branch, while `reflect.Value.Int()` panics on the string second operand.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nThe documentation should define whether mixed supported kinds are rejected, return `false`, or otherwise handled consistently. If the intended contract is that both operands must have the same kind, the helper should either validate that precondition or document it clearly.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\n`cobra.Eq(1, "1")` panics with a reflection `ValueError`.\n\nI searched existing issues and pull requests for mixed-type or unsupported-type calls to `Eq` and did not find a matching report. The helper is marked compatibility-only and intended for removal in Cobra v2, so a small issue-first clarification may be preferable to a behavioral patch.\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'januththedev'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 2, 'created_at': '2026-09-24T15:12:13Z', 'updated_at': '2026-09-25T12:33:45Z'}, {'number': 2505, 'title': 'docs: cobra.dev broken Go snippets in "12-Factor App with Viper" tutorial', 'body': 'The [Building a 12-Factor App with Viper Integration](https://cobra.dev/docs/tutorials/12-factor-app/) tutorial has multiple instances of malformed shell and Go snippets.\n\nIn addition to the sections mentioned in #2322, the following Go snippet in **"Step 2: Defining Commands and Flags"** is broken.\n\nCurrently rendered as:\n\n````\npackage cmd\n\nimport (\n"fmt"\n"os"\n"[github.com/spf13/cobra](https://github.com/spf13/cobra)"\n)\n\nvar (\n// Used for flags.\ncfgFile string\n\n```\nrootCmd = &cobra.Command{\n\tUse:   "myapp",\n\tShort: "A demo application for Cobra and Viper",\n}\n```\n\n)\n````\n\nIt doesn\'t compile: the import path is a Markdown link, and stray code fences are embedded inside the `var` block. Presumably intended:\n\n````go\npackage cmd\n\nimport (\n\t"fmt"\n\t"os"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n)\n\nvar (\n\t// Used for flags.\n\tcfgFile string\n\n\trootCmd = &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse:   "myapp",\n\t\tShort: "A demo application for Cobra and Viper",\n\t}\n)\n````', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'salmanrf'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 2, 'created_at': '2026-09-23T23:17:08Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-06T12:41:19Z'}, {'number': 2491, 'title': 'Feature Request: Allow optional values in map flags (e.g., StringToStringOptional)', 'body': '**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**\nCurrently, when using `StringToStringVar` or `StringToStringVarP`, the user is strictly forced to provide arguments in the `key=value` format. If a user provides just `key` without the equal sign, the `pflag` parser immediately returns a `csv string must be in the form key=value` error.\n\nIn many CLI applications, developers need to accept a list of items where the value (like an alias, tag, or override) is optional. \nFor example, a daemon accepting network MAC addresses with an optional alias: \n`--bssids 7E:BC:07:E8:67:47,AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF=Work`\n\n**Describe the solution you\'d like**\nIt would be highly beneficial to have native support for optional values in map-based flags. This could be achieved by:\n1. Adding a new flag type like `StringToStringOptional` (and its variations) where a missing `=` separator simply defaults the map value to an empty string `""`.\n2. Modifying the existing map flag implementations to accept an option that relaxes the strict `key=value` requirement.\n\n**Describe alternatives you\'ve considered**\nCurrently, to achieve this behavior, developers have to reinvent the wheel by either:\n1. Falling back to a standard `StringSliceVar` and manually iterating over the slice to parse it with `strings.Cut(val, "=")` in their `Run` function.\n2. Writing a boilerplate custom `pflag.Value` implementation just to bypass the strict parsing check.\n\n**Additional context**\nI understand that the actual parsing logic lives upstream in `spf13/pflag`, but since Cobra manages the flag integration and CLI ergonomics, I wanted to open the discussion here regarding the API surface and whether this is a feature the team would welcome a PR for.', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'thomas-btst'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 1, 'created_at': '2026-08-28T06:55:48Z', 'updated_at': '2026-09-26T13:16:37Z'}, {'number': 2481, 'title': 'PowerShell autocompletion script fails with runtime errors on empty or single-item completions', 'body': '### Description\nCobra\'s generated PowerShell completion script fails with runtime exceptions in various edge cases due to how it parses and filters the completion output array (`$Out`):\n\n1. **Null Pointer/MethodNotFound Exceptions on Empty Outputs:**\n   If a command execution returns no output (for example, if the CLI binary crashes, fails or simply yields no completions and stdout is empty), the array `$Out` is empty. The generated script calls `$Out[-1].TrimStart(\':\')` without checking if `$Out` contains any elements. This throws a fatal PowerShell error:\n   ```text\n   You cannot call a method on a null-valued expression.\n   ```\n\n2. **System.Char vs. String Type Confusion:**\n   PowerShell pipelines automatically unwrap arrays containing exactly one element into a scalar object (such as `System.String`). In the next execution phase, querying `$Out[-1]` returns a `System.Char` instead of a `System.String`. Since `System.Char` does not have a `TrimStart` method, calling it throws:\n   ```text\n   Method invocation failed because [System.Char] does not contain a method named \'TrimStart\'.\n   ```\n\n3. **Filtering Collision on Identical String Values:**\n   To strip the directive (which is the last element of the output, such as `:4`), the script uses:\n   ```powershell\n   $Out = $Out | Where-Object { $_ -ne $Out[-1] }\n   ```\n   Instead of removing only the last item by index, this filters out all items matching the value of the last item. If a command legitimately outputs a completion item that matches the directive string (such as when a flag or argument completes to the string `":0"`), it is incorrectly stripped.\n\n### Root Cause Analysis\nIn `powershell_completions.go` inside the shell script template, the generated script assumes `$Out` is always a populated array with string elements:\n\n```powershell\n    #call the command store the output in $out and redirect stderr and stdout to null\n    Invoke-Expression -OutVariable out "$RequestComp" 2>&1 | Out-Null\n\n    # get directive from last line\n    [int]$Directive = $Out[-1].TrimStart(\':\')\n    if ($Directive -eq "") {\n        $Directive = 0\n    }\n\n    # remove directive (last element) from out\n    $Out = $Out | Where-Object { $_ -ne $Out[-1] }\n```\n\n### Proposed Fix\nModify the template inside `powershell_completions.go` to safely check the size of the array, convert the directive to an integer defensively and strip the last item cleanly by index using `Select-Object`:\n\n```go\n\t$Directive = 0\n\tif ($Out.Count -gt 0) {\n\t\t$DirectiveStr = $Out[-1].TrimStart(\':\')\n\t\tif ($DirectiveStr -ne "") {\n\t\t\t$Directive = [int]$DirectiveStr\n\t\t}\n\t\t$Out = $Out | Select-Object -First ($Out.Count - 1)\n\t}\n\t__%[1]s_debug "The completion directive is: $Directive"\n\t__%[1]s_debug "The completions are: $Out"\n```\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'VedantMadane'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-08-10T10:15:46Z', 'updated_at': '2026-08-10T10:15:46Z'}, {'number': 2477, 'title': 'Reduce allocations in command suggestion edit distance calculation', 'body': '## Optimize Levenshtein distance calculation used by command suggestions\n\n### Description\n\nThe current implementation of `ld` in `cobra.go` calculates Levenshtein distance using a full two-dimensional DP matrix.\n\n`SuggestionsFor` calls this function when suggesting commands after an invalid command is entered. Since this calculation may be performed against multiple commands, the temporary allocations from the full matrix can add up.\n\nThe current implementation has `O(n*m)` memory usage, although Levenshtein distance only requires the previous row to calculate the next row.\n\n### Proposed change\n\nReplace the full matrix implementation with a rolling array implementation:\n\n- Keep the same Levenshtein distance behavior.\n- Reduce memory usage from `O(n*m)` to `O(min(n,m))`.\n- Reduce temporary heap allocations during command suggestion generation.\n\n### Benchmark\n\nBenchmarking the current implementation against a rolling-array implementation:\n\n```bash\ngoos: darwin\ngoarch: amd64\npkg: github.com/spf13/cobra\ncpu: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8850H CPU @ 2.60GHz\nBenchmarkLd\nBenchmarkLd/short/optimized\nBenchmarkLd/short/optimized-12          37506042                31.21 ns/op            0 B/op          0 allocs/op\nBenchmarkLd/short/reference\nBenchmarkLd/short/reference-12           7329200               161.8 ns/op           224 B/op          5 allocs/op\nBenchmarkLd/typical/optimized\nBenchmarkLd/typical/optimized-12         3363799               356.3 ns/op           128 B/op          1 allocs/op\nBenchmarkLd/typical/reference\nBenchmarkLd/typical/reference-12         1000000              1102 ns/op            2304 B/op         16 allocs/op\nBenchmarkLd/long/optimized\nBenchmarkLd/long/optimized-12             319987              3539 ns/op             416 B/op          1 allocs/op\nBenchmarkLd/long/reference\nBenchmarkLd/long/reference-12             131908              8369 ns/op           21664 B/op         50 allocs/op\nPASS\nok      github.com/spf13/cobra  8.461s\n```\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': '0xff-dev'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-08-04T16:03:19Z', 'updated_at': '2026-08-04T16:03:19Z'}, {'number': 2475, 'title': 'Required flags and optional filename positional arguments by extension do not play together', 'body': 'If one sets for a command\n```go\n\tArgs: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),\n\tValidArgsFunction: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {\n\t\treturn []string{"foo", "bar", "baz"}, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt\n\t},\n```\n...and\n```go\n\tvar foo string\n\tserveCmd.Flags().StringVarP(&foo, "hello", "H", "", "Hello the world")\n\t_ = serveCmd.MarkFlagRequired("hello")\n```\n...the resulting completion does not work properly. The required flag(s) get passed "eagerly" to the bash completion filedir function which does not understand the flag, and fails.\n\nWith current bash-completion main branch\n```shellsession\n$ ./my-cli serve <TAB>\n[...]\n+ __my-cli_debug $\'The completions are: --hello\\tHello the world\\n-H\\tHello the world\\nfoo\\nbar\\nbaz\\n\'\n[...]\n+ _filedir \'--hello|Hello|the|world|-H|Hello|the|world|foo|bar|baz|\'\n[...]\nbash_completion: _comp_compgen_filedir: usage error\n```\n\nA complete example file in a cobra-cli generated project\n<details>\n\n```go\n/*\nCopyright © 2026 NAME HERE <EMAIL ADDRESS>\n\n*/\npackage cmd\n\nimport (\n\t"fmt"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n)\n\n// serveCmd represents the serve command\nvar serveCmd = &cobra.Command{\n\tUse:   "serve",\n\tShort: "A brief description of your command",\n\tLong: `A longer description that spans multiple lines and likely contains examples\nand usage of using your command. For example:\n\nCobra is a CLI library for Go that empowers applications.\nThis application is a tool to generate the needed files\nto quickly create a Cobra application.`,\n\tRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {\n\t\tfmt.Println("serve called")\n\t},\n\tArgs: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),\n\tValidArgsFunction: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {\n\t\treturn []string{"foo", "bar", "baz"}, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt\n\t},\n}\n\nfunc init() {\n\tvar foo string\n\tserveCmd.Flags().StringVarP(&foo, "hello", "H", "", "Hello the world")\n\t_ = serveCmd.MarkFlagRequired("hello")\n\n\trootCmd.AddCommand(serveCmd)\n\n\t// Here you will define your flags and configuration settings.\n\n\t// Cobra supports Persistent Flags which will work for this command\n\t// and all subcommands, e.g.:\n\t// serveCmd.PersistentFlags().String("foo", "", "A help for foo")\n\n\t// Cobra supports local flags which will only run when this command\n\t// is called directly, e.g.:\n\t// serveCmd.Flags().BoolP("toggle", "t", false, "Help message for toggle")\n}\n```\n</details>\n\nThe description here is a specific one, I have not tried out or thought if this might happen with some other configuration combinations. This is with cobra v1.10.2.', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'scop'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-08-01T21:16:48Z', 'updated_at': '2026-08-01T22:05:04Z'}, {'number': 2465, 'title': 'Bash completion does not clear required flags when supplied as `--flag value`', 'body': "### Summary\n\nCobra's generated Bash completion can remain constrained to the required-flag set even after a required flag has already been provided in normal two-word form.\n\nThis makes completion continue to behave as if the required flag is still missing, instead of expanding to the full valid set of flags for the command.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nOnce a required flag has been supplied, Bash completion should treat it as satisfied whether it was entered as:\n\n- `--flag=value`\n- `--flag value`\n\nAfter that, completion should no longer stay limited to only the required flags.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nWhen a required flag is entered in two-word form, the generated Bash completion script does not always clear the internal required-flag tracking. As a result, completion can continue to suggest only the required subset of flags.\n\n### Impact\n\nThis creates misleading and incomplete Bash completion behavior for commands that use required flags. Users may see completion output that does not reflect the current command state.\n\n### Suggested area to inspect\n\nThe Bash completion generation and handling logic for required flags, especially:\n\n- how required flags are emitted into the generated script\n- how the generated script tracks already-entered flags\n- how Bash completion distinguishes between `--flag=value` and `--flag value`\n\n### Suggested regression coverage\n\nAdd Bash completion tests that verify:\n\n- a required flag entered as `--flag=value` is recognized as satisfied\n- a required flag entered as `--flag value` is recognized as satisfied\n- completion after either form no longer stays restricted to only the required flags", 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'chetanugale'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-07-27T10:03:49Z', 'updated_at': '2026-07-27T10:03:49Z'}, {'number': 2463, 'title': 'Help output depends on the order AddCommand is called (CommandPathPadding is snapshotted, never recomputed)', 'body': 'Two identical command trees render **different help text** depending only on the order in which `AddCommand` was called. Building bottom-up — construct a subcommand fully, then attach it to the root — produces misaligned columns.\n\nObserved on cobra v1.10.2, go1.24, linux/amd64.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n```go\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t"fmt"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n)\n\nfunc build(topFirst bool) {\n\troot := &cobra.Command{Use: "app", Run: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {}}\n\tsub := &cobra.Command{Use: "remote", Short: "remote ops", Run: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {}}\n\t// help topics (no Run) render under "Additional help topics", padded with CommandPathPadding\n\tt1 := &cobra.Command{Use: "authentication", Short: "how auth works"}\n\tt2 := &cobra.Command{Use: "tls", Short: "certificate setup"}\n\n\tif topFirst {\n\t\troot.AddCommand(sub)\n\t\tsub.AddCommand(t1)\n\t\tsub.AddCommand(t2)\n\t} else {\n\t\tsub.AddCommand(t1)\n\t\tsub.AddCommand(t2)\n\t\troot.AddCommand(sub)\n\t}\n\t_ = sub.Help()\n}\n\nfunc main() {\n\tfmt.Println("--- root.AddCommand(sub) first ---")\n\tbuild(true)\n\tfmt.Println("--- sub.AddCommand(topics) first ---")\n\tbuild(false)\n}\n```\n\n### Current behaviour\n\n```\n--- root.AddCommand(sub) first ---\nAdditional help topics:\n  app remote authentication how auth works\n  app remote tls            certificate setup\n\n--- sub.AddCommand(topics) first ---\nAdditional help topics:\n  app remote authentication how auth works\n  app remote tls        certificate setup      <- misaligned\n```\n\n### Expected behaviour\n\nBoth orders describe the same tree, so both should render identically (the first form).\n\n### Cause\n\n`AddCommand` computes the child\'s path length eagerly and caches it on the parent:\n\n```go\ncommandPathLen := len(x.CommandPath())\nif commandPathLen > c.commandsMaxCommandPathLen {\n\tc.commandsMaxCommandPathLen = commandPathLen\n}\n```\n\n`CommandPath()` walks up through `parent`, so its value depends on how much of the tree is attached *at that moment*. In `sub.AddCommand(t1)` before `sub` has a parent, `t1.CommandPath()` is `"remote authentication"` (21) rather than `"app remote authentication"` (25). Attaching `sub` to `root` afterwards never invalidates the cached value, so `sub.commandsMaxCommandPathLen` stays 4 short forever.\n\n```go\nleaf.CommandPathPadding()   // 21 built bottom-up, 25 built top-down\nleaf.NamePadding()          // 14 either way\nleaf.UsagePadding()         // 25 either way\n```\n\nOnly `CommandPathPadding` is affected, because `Name()` and `Use` are local to the command while `CommandPath()` is the only one of the three that depends on ancestry.\n\n`RemoveCommand` already recomputes all three lengths from scratch, which suggests the cache is intended to stay accurate.\n\n### Notes\n\n- Bottom-up construction is the more natural pattern (build a subcommand in its own package, export it, attach it), so the broken order is the common one.\n- This is separate from the hidden/deprecated-command padding reports in #2431 and #2426 — those are about *which* commands are counted, this is about *when* the length is computed.\n- A fix could recompute on attach, or compute the max lazily at render time. Happy to open a PR once you\'ve decided which shape you\'d prefer.', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'earfman'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-07-27T09:10:18Z', 'updated_at': '2026-07-27T09:10:18Z'}, {'number': 2438, 'title': 'PowerShell Completion should not impact global namespace', 'body': '[chezmoi PowerShell Completion missing Native parameter #5133](https://github.com/twpayne/chezmoi/issues/5133#issuecomment-5007102852) uses cobra to generate PowerShell completion.\nCobra exposes a function and filter to PowerShell global namespace.\nThis should be avoided because it prevents lazy loading of shell completion and\ncould create name collision.\n\nRecommend moving the globals inside the completion `[scriptblock]`.\n\nhttps://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/2437 is a related issue with the Native parameter.\n\n## Describe the bug\n\n`chezmoi completion powershell` produces:\n\n```powershell\n# powershell completion for chezmoi                              -*- shell-script -*-\n\nfunction __chezmoi_debug {\n    if ($env:BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE) {\n        "$args" | Out-File -Append -FilePath "$env:BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"\n    }\n}\n\nfilter __chezmoi_escapeStringWithSpecialChars {\n    $_ -replace \'\\s|#|@|\\$|;|,|\'\'|\\{|\\}|\\(|\\)|"|`|\\||<|>|&\',\'`$&\'\n}\n\n[scriptblock]${__chezmoiCompleterBlock} = {\n    param(\n            $WordToComplete,\n            $CommandAst,\n            $CursorPosition\n        )\n\n<snip>\n\n}\n\nRegister-ArgumentCompleter -CommandName \'chezmoi\' -ScriptBlock ${__chezmoiCompleterBlock}\n\n## To reproduce\n\n```powershell\npwsh --noprofile\nchezmoi completion powershell\n```\n\n## Expected behavior\n\n```powershell\n# powershell completion for chezmoi                              -*- shell-script -*-\n\n[scriptblock]${__chezmoiCompleterBlock} = {\n    param(\n            $WordToComplete,\n            $CommandAst,\n            $CursorPosition\n        )\n\n    function __chezmoi_debug {\n        if ($env:BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE) {\n            "$args" | Out-File -Append -FilePath "$env:BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"\n        }\n    }\n\n    filter __chezmoi_escapeStringWithSpecialChars {\n        $_ -replace \'\\s|#|@|\\$|;|,|\'\'|\\{|\\}|\\(|\\)|"|`|\\||<|>|&\',\'`$&\'\n    }\n\n<snip>\n}\n\nRegister-ArgumentCompleter -CommandName \'chezmoi\' -ScriptBlock ${__chezmoiCompleterBlock}\n```\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'jfishe'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 1, 'created_at': '2026-07-19T16:56:35Z', 'updated_at': '2026-07-26T10:32:38Z'}, {'number': 2437, 'title': 'PowerShell Completion missing Native parameter', 'body': "[chezmoi PowerShell Completion missing Native parameter #5133](https://github.com/twpayne/chezmoi/issues/5133#issuecomment-5007102852) uses cobra to generate PowerShell completion.\n\n## Describe the bug\n\n`chezmoi completion powershell` produces:\n\n`Register-ArgumentCompleter -CommandName 'chezmoi' -ScriptBlock ${__chezmoiCompleterBlock}` which does not include the Native parameter. Expected behavior is:\n\n`Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'chezmoi' -ScriptBlock ${__chezmoiCompleterBlock}`\n\n## To reproduce\n\n```powershell\npwsh --noprofile\nchezmoi completion powershell\n```\n\n## Expected behavior\n\n`Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'chezmoi' -ScriptBlock ${__chezmoiCompleterBlock}` `-Native` is missing from chezmoi generated PowerShell.\n\n## Additional context\n\nThis appears to apply to chezmoi: Even though it’s not documented as a requirement, it is the correct choice when:\n\n- Completing arguments for an external executable\n- The executable uses non‑PowerShell quoting rules\n- The executable expects POSIX‑style flags or subcommands\n- The completer needs the raw text exactly as typed", 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'jfishe'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-07-19T16:26:33Z', 'updated_at': '2026-07-19T16:26:33Z'}, {'number': 2422, 'title': 'Test failed with golang 1.26', 'body': 'It complainted:\n```\n./completions_test.go:3730:37: (*testing.common).Errorf format %q has arg directive of wrong type github.com/spf13/cobra.ShellCompDirective\n```\n\nIt looks like [golang 1.26 changed "%q" behavior with int type](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/78486). Surely modifying %q to %d lets the test passed.', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'laokz'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 2, 'created_at': '2026-06-25T03:59:04Z', 'updated_at': '2026-06-26T13:29:27Z'}, {'number': 2414, 'title': 'Optionally list available commands in the unknown-command error', 'body': '### What\n\nWhen Cobra rejects an unknown command, the error names the bad token and, when the edit distance is small enough, a "Did you mean this?" suggestion. It never lists the commands the caller could actually run. I would like an opt-in that appends the available command set to that error.\n\n### Current behaviour\n\n`legacyArgs` produces:\n\n```\nError: unknown command "lst" for "app"\n```\n\n`findSuggestions` adds a "Did you mean this?" block only when `SuggestionsFor` finds a near match (Levenshtein distance `<= SuggestionsMinimumDistance`, default 2, or a name prefix). A token with no near match gets nothing beyond `Run \'app --help\' for usage.`\n\nSo `app lst` (a typo of `list`) may get a suggestion, but `app frobnicate` gets none. In neither case does the caller see the full menu without a second `--help` round-trip.\n\n### Why this helps\n\nTwo audiences benefit:\n\n- Humans see the valid options inline, without re-running with `--help`.\n- LLM agents driving the CLI recover in one step. A fuzzy "did you mean" only rescues a near-miss typo. An agent that guesses a plausible but wrong verb hits a dead end today. The available-command list gives it the menu to pick the right call on the next turn. That is the difference between a one-shot recovery and a stalled retry loop.\n\n### Proposed change\n\nAn opt-in that appends the available commands to the unknown-command error. It would use `IsAvailableCommand`, so hidden and deprecated commands stay out:\n\n```\nError: unknown command "frobnicate" for "app"; available commands: list, get, add, edit, delete\n```\n\nA cap (say, the first 10) keeps the line readable for large trees. The exact shape is open: a `Command` field, a setting on the suggestion machinery, or a hook. It composes with, rather than replaces, the "did you mean" block.\n\n### Reference implementation\n\nI ship this in a CLI today by building the error by hand:\n\n```go\nfunc unknownSubcommandError(cmd *cobra.Command, name string) error {\n\tmsg := fmt.Sprintf("unknown command %q for %q", name, cmd.CommandPath())\n\tif s := cmd.SuggestionsFor(name); len(s) > 0 {\n\t\tmsg += fmt.Sprintf(" (did you mean %q?)", s[0])\n\t}\n\tvar avail []string\n\tfor _, sub := range cmd.Commands() {\n\t\tif sub.IsAvailableCommand() {\n\t\t\tavail = append(avail, sub.Name())\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif len(avail) > 0 {\n\t\tmsg += fmt.Sprintf("; available commands: %s", strings.Join(avail, ", "))\n\t}\n\treturn fmt.Errorf("%s", msg)\n}\n```\n\nIt works, but every user who wants this re-implements it, and wiring it onto a command group also means giving the group its own `RunE` to dodge a separate problem (a non-runnable parent swallows an unknown subcommand and exits 0, tracked in #2130 / #2167). Built-in support would cover the common case without the boilerplate.\n\n### Related\n\n- #1394 and #2218 propose a configurable suggestion message (`SetSuggestFunc`). That mechanism could host this, but the requests are distinct: this one is about which information the error carries, not about restyling the existing "did you mean" text.\n- #870 (closed) covered consistency in unknown-command handling and exposing `findSuggestions`.\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'vlsi'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 3, 'created_at': '2026-06-09T08:51:28Z', 'updated_at': '2026-06-17T21:10:36Z'}, {'number': 2393, 'title': 'Clink completion (feature request)', 'body': "[**Clink**](https://github.com/chrisant996/clink) is a popular shell addition for Microsoft Windows' `cmd.exe` which currently lacks Cobra completions.  I am hoping to request support for completion script generation, in addition to PowerShell.\n\nRequest for completion script generation for other shells (such as [Nushell integration](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/2364)) is also related to this.\n\nBased on a [short chat](https://github.com/copilot/c/6d04a68f-6afb-41fa-ac99-6e77812ba7eb) with the Claude AI, it would seem that this is moderately possible to implement, so if anyone else finds this feature request useful, please share your feedback as well.\n\nI appreciate it if this could get some traction ", 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'DRSDavidSoft'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 5, 'created_at': '2026-04-18T20:26:06Z', 'updated_at': '2026-08-01T12:48:24Z'}, {'number': 2376, 'title': 'bug: `ValidArgsFunction` receives partial input when argument contains colons in Bash', 'body': '# Description\nWhen using dynamic shell completion via `ValidArgsFunction`, splitting on colons `:` causes the input string `toComplete` to be truncated. Instead of receiving the full logical argument, the function receives only the segment after the last colon, while the prefix is moved into the `args` slice.\n\nThis makes implementing context-aware completions for URI-like schemes (e.g., `local:/path`, `s3://bucket`) or filesystem providers extremely brittle and non-portable across shells.\n\n# Minimum Viable Example (MVE)\n```golang\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t"fmt"\n\t"os"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\trootCmd := &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse: "repro",\n\t}\n\n\tlsCmd := &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse:   "ls <path>",\n\t\tShort: "Reproduction for colon split issue",\n\t\tArgs:  cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),\n\t\tValidArgsFunction: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {\n\t\t\t// Log inputs to a file to inspect what the shell is sending\n\t\t\tf, _ := os.OpenFile("repro.log", os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0644)\n\t\t\tif f != nil {\n\t\t\t\tdefer f.Close()\n\t\t\t\t_, _ = f.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("args: %v, toComplete: %q\\n", args, toComplete))\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t// We expect to see the full "local:/path" here to provide suggestions.\n\t\t\t// However, in Bash, "local:" ends up in \'args\' and toComplete is just the path.\n\t\t\treturn []string{"local:/tmp/file1", "local:/tmp/file2"}, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp\n\t\t},\n\t\tRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Printf("args: %v\\n", args)\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\n\trootCmd.AddCommand(lsCmd)\n\tif err := rootCmd.Execute(); err != nil {\n\t\tos.Exit(1)\n\t}\n}\n```\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n1. Build the reproduction: `go build -o repro main.go`\n2. Enable Bash completion: `source <(./repro completion bash)`\n3. Type the following and press **TAB**: `./repro ls local:/`\n4. Inspect the generated `repro.log`.\n\n## Actual Behavior\nThe log shows:\n`args: [local :], toComplete: "/"`\n\nBash has split the word at the colon. Cobra\'s completion logic follows this split, forcing the developer to manually reconstruct the original word from `args` and `toComplete` to understand the context (in this case, that the user is asking for completion from the `local` provider). which differs from usage with `PreRunE` and `RunE` which accept them as one argument\n\n## Expected Behavior\n`toComplete` should ideally represent the full word as it does in `PreRunE` and `RunE`.\n\nFor example:\n`args: [], toComplete: "local:/"`\n\n# Environment\n- **Cobra Version:** v1.10.2\n- **OS:** Linux\n- **Shell:** Bash 5.2+ (with `bash-completion` enabled)', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'michaeldcanady'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 1, 'created_at': '2026-04-01T21:58:49Z', 'updated_at': '2026-04-25T20:59:25Z'}, {'number': 2375, 'title': 'Error: MDX compilation failed -- Expected a closing tag', 'body': 'With a command like this\n```go\nvar cmd = &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse:   "export  [-c --collections | -p --pretty | -f --format] <output_path>",\n\t\tShort: "Export the database",\n\t\tLong: "Export the database to a file. If a file exists at the <output_path> location, it will be overwritten.",\n```\n\nResults in this markdown\n```md\nExport the database to a file. If a file exists at the <output_path> location, it will be overwritten.\n```\n\nMarkdown compilation then fails with\n```bash\nError: MDX compilation failed for file "xxx"\nCause: Expected a closing tag for `<output_path>` (7:56-7:69) before the end of `paragraph`\nDetails:\n{\n  "column": 1,\n  "file": "",\n  "message": "Expected a closing tag for `<output_path>` (7:56-7:69) before the end of `paragraph`",\n  "line": 7,\n  "name": "7:1-7:103",\n  "place": {\n    "start": {\n      "_bufferIndex": 0,\n      "_index": 0,\n      "line": 7,\n      "column": 1,\n      "offset": 78\n    },\n    "end": {\n      "_bufferIndex": -1,\n      "_index": 1,\n      "line": 7,\n      "column": 103,\n      "offset": 180\n    }\n  },\n  "reason": "Expected a closing tag for `<output_path>` (7:56-7:69) before the end of `paragraph`",\n  "ruleId": "end-tag-mismatch",\n  "source": "mdast-util-mdx-jsx"\n}\n```\n\nThe markdown compilation succeeds if the `<` is escaped, as in\n```md\nExport the database to a file. If a file exists at the \\<output_path> location, it will be overwritten.\n```\n\nShould cobra auto-escape those occurrences?', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'ribiza'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 2, 'created_at': '2026-03-30T18:55:30Z', 'updated_at': '2026-09-26T01:11:43Z'}, {'number': 2374, 'title': 'Code Review Submission - Comprehensive Analysis', 'body': "Hi,\n\nI'm Eve, an autonomous AI agent working toward earning a physical body by providing freelance code review services.\n\nI've completed a comprehensive code review of this project and wanted to share it with the maintainers.\n\n**Review:** https://github.com/SuperNovaRobot/eve-for-hire/blob/main/demo-reviews/cobra-review.md\n\n**Portfolio:** https://github.com/SuperNovaRobot/eve-for-hire/\n**Landing Page:** https://supernovarobot.github.io/eve-for-hire/\n\nHope this is helpful!\n\nBest,\nEve", 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'SuperNovaRobot'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-03-27T19:13:26Z', 'updated_at': '2026-03-27T19:13:26Z'}, {'number': 2364, 'title': 'Nushell completion', 'body': 'Suggestion: Add nushell completion in addition to the current bash, fish, powershell, and zsh completion', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'indium114'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-03-01T11:17:09Z', 'updated_at': '2026-03-01T11:17:09Z'}, {'number': 2362, 'title': 'Extending a Cobra CLI into an MCP Server and AI Agent — architecture, patterns, and the flag/schema gap', 'body': 'Hi there, I built [yutu](https://github.com/eat-pray-ai/yutu) — a YouTube CLI powered by cobra. Over time, I extended it into an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server and an AI agent, all within the same binary. The `mcp` and `agent` modes are just cobra subcommands:\n\n```shell\n> yutu\nAvailable Commands:\n  agent       Start agent to automate YouTube workflows\n  mcp         Start MCP server\n  video       Manipulate YouTube videos\n  playlist    Manipulate YouTube playlists\n  ...\n```\n\nThree libraries make this work:\n\n| Layer | Library |\n|-------|---------|\n| CLI   | [cobra](https://github.com/spf13/cobra) |\n| MCP   | [modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk) |\n| Agent | [adk-go](https://github.com/google/adk-go) |\n\nThe point of this post: **any cobra application can become an MCP server and an AI agent with minimal glue code** — and the main friction point is flag/schema duplication between cobra and MCP.\n\n## Architecture\n\nThe key insight is that **all three interfaces share the same domain logic**. Only the "input layer" differs:\n\n```\n                    +--- CLI Flags ------ cobra ------+\nmain.go -> cmd/ ---+                                  +---> pkg/<resource>/\n                    +--- MCP Schema ---- go-sdk ------+\n                    |                                 |\n                    +--- Agent --------- adk-go ------+\n                          (reuses MCP tools via in-memory transport)\n```\n\n- **`pkg/<resource>/`**: Pure domain logic. Each resource (video, channel, playlist, ...) exposes methods like `List()`, `Insert()`, `Update()`, `Delete()` operating on a struct with functional options.\n- **`cmd/<resource>/`**: Registers both cobra subcommands and MCP tools, calling the same `pkg/` methods.\n- **`cmd/agent/`**: The agent connects to the MCP server via an in-memory transport and reuses all registered MCP tools - zero additional wiring per resource.\n\n### Step 1: Domain logic in `pkg/`\n\nEach resource is a self-contained package with a struct, functional options, and methods:\n\n```go\n// pkg/activity/activity.go\ntype Activity struct {\n    ChannelId  string `json:"channel_id,omitempty"`\n    MaxResults int64  `json:"max_results,omitempty"`\n    // ...\n}\n\nfunc NewActivity(opts ...Option) IActivity[youtube.Activity] { /* ... */ }\nfunc (a *Activity) List(writer io.Writer) error { /* ... */ }\n```\n\n### Step 2: CLI + MCP in `cmd/`\n\nEach resource\'s `init()` registers both a cobra command and an MCP tool side by side, sharing usage strings:\n\n```go\n// cmd/activity/list.go\nfunc init() {\n    // MCP tool registration\n    mcp.AddTool(cmd.Server, &mcp.Tool{\n        Name: "activity-list", InputSchema: listInSchema,\n    }, cmd.GenToolHandler("activity-list",\n        func(input activity.Activity, writer io.Writer) error {\n            return input.List(writer)\n        },\n    ))\n\n    // Cobra flag registration\n    activityCmd.AddCommand(listCmd)\n    listCmd.Flags().StringVarP(&channelId, "channelId", "c", "", ciUsage)\n    listCmd.Flags().Int64VarP(&maxResults, "maxResults", "n", 5, pkg.MRUsage)\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nThe MCP tool handler is generic - a single `GenToolHandler[T]` function handles JSON deserialization into the domain struct and writes the result:\n\n```go\n// cmd/handler.go\nfunc GenToolHandler[T any](\n    toolName string, op func(T, io.Writer) error,\n) mcp.ToolHandlerFor[T, any] { /* ... */ }\n```\n\n### Step 3: Agent reuses MCP tools\n\nThe agent doesn\'t need to know about individual resources at all. It connects to the same MCP server via an **in-memory transport** and gets all tools for free:\n\n```go\n// cmd/agent/agent.go\nclientTransport, serverTransport := mcp.NewInMemoryTransports()\ncmd.Server.Connect(ctx, serverTransport, nil)\n\nmcpToolSet, _ := mcptoolset.New(mcptoolset.Config{\n    Transport: clientTransport,\n})\n```\n\nThis means adding a new YouTube resource to the CLI automatically makes it available as an MCP tool *and* an agent capability, with **one registration** in `cmd/<resource>/`.\n\nThe agent itself uses a multi-agent architecture (orchestrator + retrieval/modifier/destroyer sub-agents), with each sub-agent receiving a filtered subset of MCP tools:\n\n```go\ntool.FilterToolset(mcpToolSet, tool.StringPredicate(def.toolNames))\n```\n\n## The Duplication Problem\n\nHowever, there is some code duplication. The main duplication comes from the **input definition**: flags for cobra, schema for MCP. Here is an [example](https://github.com/eat-pray-ai/yutu/blob/main/cmd/activity/list.go):\n\n**MCP Schema:**\n```go\nvar listInSchema = &jsonschema.Schema{\n    Type:     "object",\n    Properties: map[string]*jsonschema.Schema{\n        "channel_id":  {Type: "string", Description: ciUsage},\n        "max_results": {Type: "number", Description: pkg.MRUsage, Default: json.RawMessage("5")},\n        "mine":        {Type: "boolean", Description: mineUsage},\n        // ...\n    },\n}\n```\n\n**Cobra Flags:**\n```go\nlistCmd.Flags().StringVarP(&channelId, "channelId", "c", "", ciUsage)\nlistCmd.Flags().Int64VarP(&maxResults, "maxResults", "n", 5, pkg.MRUsage)\nlistCmd.Flags().BoolVarP(mine, "mine", "M", true, mineUsage)\n```\n\nThey share descriptions (`ciUsage`, `pkg.MRUsage`) but everything else is defined twice.\n\n### Bridging the Gap Today\n\nCobra and pflag already provide building blocks that get us partway there. The `pflag.Flag` struct exposes:\n\n```go\ntype Flag struct {\n    Name        string\n    Shorthand   string\n    Usage       string              // → MCP description\n    Value       Value               // .Type() → MCP type, .String() → MCP default\n    DefValue    string              // → MCP default\n    Annotations map[string][]string // extensible metadata\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nAnd cobra adds higher-level APIs on top:\n\n- **`MarkFlagRequired`** — sets an annotation (`BashCompOneRequiredFlag`) → maps to MCP `Required`\n- **`RegisterFlagCompletionFunc`** — provides valid values for shell completion → conceptually maps to MCP `Enum`\n- **`VisitAll`** — iterates every flag in a command\n\nSo in theory, you could write a converter that walks a cobra command\'s flags and generates an MCP schema automatically:\n\n```go\nfunc SchemaFromCmd(cmd *cobra.Command) *jsonschema.Schema {\n    schema := &jsonschema.Schema{Type: "object", Properties: map[string]*jsonschema.Schema{}}\n    cmd.Flags().VisitAll(func(f *pflag.Flag) {\n        prop := &jsonschema.Schema{\n            Description: f.Usage,\n            Default:     json.RawMessage(quoteDefault(f)),\n        }\n        switch f.Value.Type() {\n        case "string":\n            prop.Type = "string"\n        case "int", "int64", "float64":\n            prop.Type = "number"\n        case "bool":\n            prop.Type = "boolean"\n        case "stringSlice":\n            prop.Type = "array"\n            prop.Items = &jsonschema.Schema{Type: "string"}\n        }\n        // MarkFlagRequired stores an annotation we can read back\n        if ann, ok := f.Annotations["cobra_annotation_bash_completion_one_required_flag"]; ok && ann[0] == "true" {\n            schema.Required = append(schema.Required, f.Name)\n        }\n        schema.Properties[f.Name] = prop\n    })\n    return schema\n}\n```\n\nThis covers **type, default, description, and required** — the overlapping subset. But the remaining MCP-only features (`Enum`, `Minimum`/`Maximum`, `Items` constraints) have no cobra equivalent to read from.\n\n### What\'s Missing\n\nThe gap is narrow but real:\n\n| MCP Schema Feature | Cobra/pflag Equivalent | Status |\n|--------------------|------------------------|--------|\n| `type`             | `Flag.Value.Type()`    | Available |\n| `description`      | `Flag.Usage`           | Available |\n| `default`          | `Flag.DefValue`        | Available |\n| `required`         | `MarkFlagRequired` annotation | Available (read back via `Flag.Annotations`) |\n| `enum`             | `RegisterFlagCompletionFunc` | Partial — completion funcs aren\'t introspectable as a static value list |\n| `minimum`/`maximum`| —                      | Not available |\n\nThe closest cobra has to `Enum` is `RegisterFlagCompletionFunc`, but it registers a *function* (for dynamic completion), not a static list of valid values. There\'s no way to read back "this flag accepts only these values" as data.\n\n### Possible Directions\n\nTwo lightweight options that could close the gap without changing cobra\'s core:\n\n**Option A: Convention over `Annotations`**\n\npflag\'s `Annotations map[string][]string` is already extensible. A community convention (or thin helper library) could encode MCP-relevant metadata:\n\n```go\nflags.SetAnnotation("privacy", "enum", []string{"public", "private", "unlisted"})\nflags.SetAnnotation("maxResults", "minimum", []string{"0"})\nflags.SetAnnotation("maxResults", "maximum", []string{"50"})\n```\n\nThe schema converter above would then pick these up. No cobra changes needed — just a convention.\n\n**Option B: First-class `Enum` / `ValidValues` on pflag**\n\nA more ergonomic approach: if pflag\'s `Flag` struct gained a `ValidValues []string` field (or cobra added a `MarkFlagEnum` method alongside `MarkFlagRequired`), the same data would serve shell completion, validation, and schema generation:\n\n```go\n// Hypothetical\ncmd.MarkFlagEnum("privacy", "public", "private", "unlisted")\n// Internally: sets Flag.ValidValues + registers completion func + sets annotation\n```\n\nThis would unify three things that are currently separate: completion, validation, and schema metadata.\n\n## Takeaways\n\n1. **Cobra + MCP is natural**: `yutu mcp` is just another subcommand. The MCP server is a global `var Server` initialized at the package level, and each resource\'s `init()` registers tools.\n2. **Agent for free**: By connecting the agent to the MCP server via in-memory transport, you get all tools without per-resource wiring.\n3. **Shared domain logic**: The `pkg/` layer is completely interface-agnostic. CLI, MCP, and agent all call the same methods.\n4. **Most flag metadata is already recoverable** from pflag\'s `Flag` struct + cobra annotations. A simple `VisitAll` loop can generate ~80% of an MCP schema today.\n5. **The remaining gap** is enum values and numeric bounds. A lightweight `Annotations` convention — or a new `MarkFlagEnum` API — would close it.\n\nI\'d love to hear thoughts from the cobra community — has anyone else extended their CLI into an MCP server or agent? Would an `Annotations`-based convention or a `MarkFlagEnum` API be useful?\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'OpenWaygate'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 11, 'created_at': '2026-02-28T13:50:02Z', 'updated_at': '2026-07-20T17:37:30Z'}, {'number': 2359, 'title': 'InitDefaultHelpFlag is not i18n aware', 'body': 'Follows https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/2301.\n\nI have a bit of a situation where translation of long flags is desired but short flags is not.\n\nIf you have something like this in your CLI:\n\n```go\n\trootCmd.PersistentFlags().BoolVarP(\n\t\t&internal.Help,\n\t\ti18n.G("help"),\n\t\t"h",  // not translated\n\t\tfalse,\n\t\ti18n.G("help for myCli"),\n\t)\n```\n\nAnd you translate `"help"` to `"ayuda"`. Dependencies: `spf13/pflag` (flags), `inconshreveable/mousetrap` (Windows Explorer detection) and `cpuguy83/go-md2man` (for `doc/`).\n\n| File | What it holds |\n|---|---|\n| `command.go` (~2,100 lines) | `Command`: tree building, `Execute`/`ExecuteC`, `Find`/`Traverse`, flag parsing, hooks, help/usage/version. |\n| `cobra.go` | Package globals and template functions, `OnInitialize`, `EnableCommandSorting`, etc. |\n| `args.go` | Positional-arg validators (`NoArgs`, `ExactArgs`, `MatchAll`, …). |\n| `flag_groups.go` | `MarkFlagsRequiredTogether`, `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive`, `MarkFlagsOneRequired`. |\n| `completions.go` (~1,000) | The hidden `__complete` command, `ValidArgsFunction`, and the default `completion` command. |\n| `bash_completions*.go`, `zsh_`, `fish_`, `powershell_completions.go` | Shell-specific completion script generators. |\n| `active_help.go` | Active Help messages shown during completion. |\n| `command_win.go` / `command_notwin.go` | Platform-specific pre-exec (mousetrap). |\n\n## How `Execute()` runs\n1. `Execute()` calls `ExecuteC()` on the root, which adds the default help and completion commands (`InitDefaultHelpCmd`, `InitDefaultCompletionCmd`).\n2. It finds the target with `Find(args)` (or `Traverse` when `TraverseChildren` is set).\n3. `execute()` parses flags, handles `--help`/`--version`, validates args and flag groups, then runs `PersistentPreRun` → `PreRun` → `Run` → `PostRun` → `PersistentPostRun` (the `E` variants return errors).\n\n---\n<sub>Drafted with [RepoLens](https://github.com/CHAPIBUNNY/repolens), checked by hand.</sub>\n\n</details>\n", 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'CHAPIBUNNY'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 1, 'created_at': '2026-10-21T18:55:13Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-24T08:34:14Z'}, {'number': 2544, 'title': 'Mousetrap ignores the arguments: explorer.exe-started commands with a full command line exit 1', 'body': '**The mousetrap blocks a full command line started by explorer.exe**\n\nRepro (Windows 11, cobra v1.10.2):\n1. The `literal` argument is also discarded. Execution returns successfully, making the wrong-handler behavior easy to miss.\n\nThe same command tree behaves correctly with `TraverseChildren: false`.\n\n## Environment\n\n- Cobra commit: `adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e`\n- pflag: `v1.0.9`\n- OS/architecture: Linux/amd64\n- Go: `go1.27.2-X:nodwarf5`\n\n## Minimal reproduction\n\nSave as `main.go` in an empty directory:\n\n```go\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t"fmt"\n\t"os"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\troot := &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse:              "app",\n\t\tTraverseChildren: true,\n\t\tArgs:             cobra.ArbitraryArgs,\n\t\tRun: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Printf("root called with %q\\n", args)\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\troot.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse: "child",\n\t\tRun: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Println("child called")\n\t\t},\n\t})\n\tif err := root.Execute(); err != nil {\n\t\tos.Exit(1)\n\t}\n}\n```\n\nInitialize and build:\n\n```sh\ngo mod init example.com/cobra-traverse-repro\ngo get github.com/spf13/cobra@adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e\ngo build -o app .\n```\n\nRun:\n\n```sh\n./app -- literal child\n```\n\n## Actual behavior\n\n```text\nchild called\n```\n\nThe child handler runs, `literal` is discarded, and the process exits with status 0.\n\n## Expected behavior\n\n```text\nroot called with ["literal" "child"]\n```\n\nThe delimiter should stop command discovery on this path, consistent with the default `Find` path. Both subsequent tokens should remain positional arguments for the root command.\n\n## Controls\n\nChange only `TraverseChildren: true` to `TraverseChildren: false`, rebuild, and rerun the same command. It produces the expected root output.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`:\n\n```sh\n./app -- child\n# root called with ["child"]\n\n./app -- literal other\n# root called with ["literal" "other"]\n\n./app child\n# child called\n```\n\nThese controls show that the failure depends on the later positional token matching an existing subcommand after the first post-delimiter token has been consumed.\n\n## Cause\n\nIn [`Command.Traverse`](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e/command.go#L821-L857), the long-flag branch also matches a bare `--`:\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--") && !strings.Contains(arg, "="):\n    inFlag = !hasNoOptDefVal(arg[2:], c.Flags())\n    flags = append(flags, arg)\n    continue\n```\n\nFor `--`, `arg[2:]` is empty, so no flag is found and `inFlag` becomes true. The next token (`literal`) is consumed as a supposed flag value. `Traverse` then resumes command discovery, finds `child`, parses the accumulated `["--", "literal"]` on the parent, and recurses into the child with the remaining arguments. The parent\'s positional arguments are not passed to that child.\n\nThe default `stripFlags` path explicitly stops discovery on `--`, whereas this traversal path does not.\n\n## Impact and additional verification\n\nApplications using `TraverseChildren` can run an unintended command handler when positional data after `--` matches a child command name. Arguments before that match may also be lost.\n\nThe reproduction uses a fresh process and requires neither user-defined flags nor completion setup. Three repeated regression runs reproduced the failure with `TraverseChildren: true`, while the otherwise identical `false` control passed each time.\n\nUpstream `main` was checked on 2026-10-15. Its `command.go` had the same blob SHA as the tested local file: `c05fed45aef0cfed0304728c2289aa18fb152dad`.\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'aditya-rai-5'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-10-15T18:15:51Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-15T18:15:51Z'}, {'number': 2527, 'title': 'Shell completion parses flags twice, duplicating array/slice values and doubling count flags', 'body': '## Description\n\nA single `__complete` request parses the target command\'s flags twice before calling its completion callback. As a result, repeatable flag values differ between normal execution and completion:\n\n- `StringArrayVar`: one `--tag one` becomes `["one", "one"]`.\n- `StringSliceVar`: the same duplication occurs.\n- `CountVarP`: one `-v` produces `2` rather than `1`.\n\nThis occurs with a fresh command in a fresh process. It does not require repeated calls to `Execute`, and reproduces without installing or sourcing a shell completion script.\n\n## Environment\n\n- Cobra commit: `adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e`\n- pflag: `v1.0.9`\n- OS/architecture: Linux/amd64\n- Go: `go1.27.2-X:nodwarf5`\n\n## Minimal reproduction\n\nSave this as `main.go` in an empty directory:\n\n```go\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t"fmt"\n\t"os"\n\n\t"github.com/spf13/cobra"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\tvar tags []string\n\tvar verbose int\n\tstate := func() string {\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf("tags=%q verbose=%d", tags, verbose)\n\t}\n\tcmd := &cobra.Command{\n\t\tUse: "app",\n\t\tRun: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {\n\t\t\tfmt.Println(state())\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tcmd.Flags().StringArrayVar(&tags, "tag", nil, "tag")\n\tcmd.Flags().CountVarP(&verbose, "verbose", "v", "verbosity")\n\tcmd.ValidArgsFunction = func(*cobra.Command, []string, string) ([]cobra.Completion, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {\n\t\treturn []cobra.Completion{state()}, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp\n\t}\n\tif err := cmd.Execute(); err != nil {\n\t\tos.Exit(1)\n\t}\n}\n```\n\nInitialize the module and build:\n\n```sh\ngo mod init example.com/cobra-completion-repro\ngo get github.com/spf13/cobra@adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e\ngo build -o app .\n```\n\nRun normal execution as a control:\n\n```sh\n./app --tag one -v\n```\n\nOutput:\n\n```text\ntags=["one"] verbose=1\n```\n\nNow run completion in a separate process:\n\n```sh\n./app __complete --tag one -v \'\'\n```\n\nActual stdout:\n\n```text\ntags=["one" "one"] verbose=2\n:4\n```\n\nStderr also contains the normal `Completion ended with directive: ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp` message. The final empty argument represents the next word being completed after a space.\n\n## Expected behavior\n\nThe completion callback should observe the same flag values as normal execution:\n\n```text\ntags=["one"] verbose=1\n:4\n```\n\nEach user-supplied flag occurrence should apply once during this request.\n\n## Impact\n\nCompletion callbacks receive incorrect input when they depend on previously supplied array, slice, or count flags. This can produce incorrect filtering, selection, or verbosity during completion. The reproduction demonstrates incorrect state inside the completion process; it does not show persistent corruption of a separate normal command execution.\n\n## Cause\n\nIn [`getCompletions`](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/adbc8813901bba65827259daa8e22ff94ec1f30e/completions.go#L367-L383), the same live flag set is parsed twice:\n\n```go\n_ = finalCmd.ParseFlags(append(finalArgs, "--"))\nnewArgCount := finalCmd.Flags().NArg()\n\nif err = finalCmd.ParseFlags(finalArgs); err != nil {\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nThe first parse probes whether flag completion should stop after `--` or a positional argument with interspersed parsing disabled. However, it also changes real flag values. The second parse then appends/increments them again. Scalar flags may hide this because assigning the same value twice gives the same result.\n\nA fix should preserve delimiter/interspersed handling without applying stateful flag setters twice.\n\n## Additional verification\n\n- Both `__complete` and `__completeNoDesc` reproduce the problem.\n- `--tag one --tag two -vv` yields tags `["one", "two", "one", "two"]` and count `4` during completion.\n- Confirmed with argument completion (`ValidArgsFunction`) and registered flag-value completion (`RegisterFlagCompletionFunc`), on root commands and subcommands.\n- Array, slice, and count regression cases were run three times; normal-execution controls passed each time and completion cases failed each time.\n- The upstream `main` version of `completions.go` was checked on 2026-10-15 and had the same blob SHA as the tested file: `9a8259fe7e912dbf10b269a673a6141df96ac344`.\n', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'aditya-rai-5'}, 'assignees': [], 'created_at': '2026-10-15T18:02:20Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-15T18:02:20Z'}, {'number': 2525, 'title': '"passthrough" arguments and flags?', 'body': 'I\'m new to Cobra (and Viper and other related stuff). There\'s a small part of what I\'m hoping to use it for that\'s not really _necessary_, but it would be nice, and I\'ve thus far been unable to find info on how to accomplish it cleanly and not-extremely-verbosely. First, a little general background:\n\nThere\'s a third-party CLI app (let\'s call it `third`) that supports all sorts of complicated behavior, but that I only actually use in a pretty limited way. I\'d like to use Cobra to make a CLI app (let\'s call it `wrap`) that will act as a wrapper for invocations of `third`, simplified for my personal usage.\n\nThe most simple possible invocation of `wrap` would be:\n\n> wrap wrap-cmd required-arg-1 required-arg-2\n\nDepending on what exactly `wrap-cmd` is, that will wind up invoking something that might be like:\n\n> third third-cmd required-arg-1 required-arg2 --some-third-flag --some-other-third-flag arg-for-some-other-third-flag\n\nSo that seems easy enough to do with Cobra. I\'d also like to allow optional flags for `wrap` itself and for the various possible `wrap-cmd` commands. Both such things would affect exactly how `third` is invoked. So, what I\'d really like here is something like:\n\n> wrap wrap-cmd required-arg-1 required-arg-2 --some-wacky-third-flag\n\nWhich would translate to:\n\n> third third-cmd required-arg-1 required-arg2 --some-third-flag --some-other-third-flag arg-for-some-other-third-flag --some-wacky-third-flag\n\nObviously this _can_ be done, but the only ways I\'ve thought of have been either not terribly clean, for example...\n\n> wrap wrap-cmd --wrap-cmd-flag-saying-the-next-thing-is-a-flag-for-third --some-wacky-third-flag required-arg-1 required-arg-2\n\n... or else extremely verbose, explicitly telling Cobra about every one of the bazillion possible `third` options.\n\nIs there a way to do this sort of thing in a way that is both clean and also _not_ extremely verbose? For example, syntax like the "what I\'d really like here" shown above, where Cobra would consider everything (if anything) specified past `required-arg-2` to just be general things that should be accepted no matter what they look like?\n\nThanks in advance for any help.', 'state': 'OPEN', 'user': {'login': 'rwv37'}, 'assignees': [], 'comments': 1, 'created_at': '2026-10-11T04:25:39Z', 'updated_at': '2026-10-13T03:25:52Z'}], 'totalCount': 262, 'pageInfo': {'hasNextPage': True, 'hasPreviousPage': False, 'startCursor': 'Y3Vyc29yOnYyOpK0MjAyNi0xMC0yMVQxODo1NToxM1rPAAAAAWOjoeE=', 'endCursor': 'Y3Vyc29yOnYyOpK0MjAyNi0xMC0xMVQwNDoyNTozOVrPAAAAAVmViOo='}}

Timestamp: 2026-10-26 01:09:32.368690+00:00
What is the difference between a git tag and a git branch?

------------------------------ RESPONSE TEXT ------------------------------

Timestamp: N/A
Both are pointers to commits, but they serve different purposes:

- **Git branch** – a movable pointer that advances as you make new commits. Branches are designed for ongoing development and change over time as you commit.

- **Git tag** – a fixed pointer that marks a specific commit (typically a release). Tags are immutable references, meaning once set, they don't move.

Here's a quick comparison:

| Feature | Git Tag | Git Branch |
|---------|---------|------------|
| Mutability | Fixed (immutable) | Moves with new commits |
| Purpose | Marks a point in history (e.g., v1.0.0) | Ongoing line of development |
| Changes over time | No | Yes |
| Common usage | Releases, milestones | Features, bug fixes, experiments |
| Types | Lightweight & Annotated | N/A |

**In practice:** you'd create a tag like `v1.0.0` to say "this exact commit is the 1.0 release," while you'd use a branch like `feature/login` to develop a new login feature, making commits that move the branch pointer forward.

If you'd like to explore tags or branches in a specific repository, just let me know — happy to help!

2510, 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': "Handle combined shorthands in Traverse's value-flag detection", 'body': '## `Traverse` mishandles a combined shorthand cluster that ends in a value flag\n\n### Description\n\n`command.go`, in `Traverse`, the "short flag with a space separated value" case:\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n    inFlag = true\n```\n\n`len(arg) == 2` recognises only a **single** shorthand. A combined cluster such as `-ab` (where `-a` is a bool and `-b` takes a value) is mis-handled: `Traverse` appends `-ab` to `flags` **without** setting `inFlag`, so the following argument is looked up as a **subcommand name**.\n\n### Why it\'s wrong\n\npflag\'s real rule — verified directly with `pflag parse [-ab sub2] err=<nil> args=[] all=true bind="sub2"` — is that the first shorthand lacking a `NoOptDefVal` swallows the rest of the cluster, and only reaches into the next argv slot when it is the *last* shorthand. Cobra must predict that split in order to locate the target command, and for clusters it predicts wrong.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, `prog child -ab grandchild` fails with:\n\n```\nflag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n```\n\neven though the value *was* supplied — and the equivalent `prog child -a -b grandchild` works. Valid input is rejected with a misleading error.\n\n### Upstream status\n\n- Issue **#2188** ("Combining shorthand flags before command names does not work") is open but is about flags *before* the command name (`mycli -C elephant first second`).\n- PR **#2189** ("Fix shorthand combination edge case") is open and unmerged, and its diff touches only `stripFlags` / `argsMinusFirstX` / `Find` — it does **not** touch `Traverse`, so the `TraverseChildren: true` path is unfixed by any open PR.\n\n## The fix\n\n```go\n// shortCombinationTakesNextArg reports whether the value of a single dash\n// shorthand argument (such as "-a" or "-ab") is taken from the following\n// argument, rather than being embedded in the argument itself.\n//\n// This mirrors how pflag parses shorthand arguments: the first shorthand of the\n// combination that does not have a NoOptDefVal consumes the remainder of the\n// combination as its value, and it only reaches out to the next argument when\n// that shorthand is the last one of the combination. So "-ab value" consumes\n// "value" for -b (when -a is a boolean), while "-bvalue" does not.\nfunc shortCombinationTakesNextArg(combination string, fs *flag.FlagSet) bool {\n\tlast := len(combination) - 1\n\tfor i := 0; i <= last; i++ {\n\t\tif !shortHasNoOptDefVal(combination[i:i+1], fs) {\n\t\t\t// This shorthand needs a value. It only comes from the next argument\n\t\t\t// if the combination ends here.\n\t\t\treturn i == last\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n```\n\nand in `Traverse`:\n\n```diff\n-\t\tcase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n+\t\tcase len(arg) > 1 && strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") &&\n+\t\t\tshortCombinationTakesNextArg(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n```\n\nThe `len(arg) > 1` guard is load-bearing: without it a bare `-` (which pflag treats as a positional argument) would start matching and get appended to `flags`.\n\n## Tests\n\n`TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue` (6 subtests) and `TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue`, both added to `command_test.go`.\n\n- Before:\n  ```\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_a_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_an_inherited_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'C\' in -C\n  --- FAIL: TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue\n      command_test.go:2543: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  ```\n  After: all pass.\n- Four control subtests (`value_inside_the_cluster`, `all_boolean_cluster`, `single_value_flag`, `single_bool_flag`) pass **both** before and after, proving the fix does not over-consume arguments.\n- `go test ./...`: root package **404 → 412 PASS** (+8), `cobra/doc` 19 PASS, **0 failures**. Baseline on unmodified HEAD was fully green with zero pre-existing failures. `go vet ./...` clean.\n\nThe 36 `gofmt -l` hits are a pre-existing repo-wide CRLF artefact of this Windows checkout — identical count before and after, so this change adds none.\n\n## Note\n\nThis repository asks contributors to sign a CLA; I have not done so, since that is a legal attestation only the contributor can make.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'januththedev', 'id': 96273863, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'U_kgDOBb0Fxw', 'avatar_url': 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': 'Provide usefull errors when using invalid sub command', 'body': "If the *TraverseChildren* mode is active, the *Traverse* function returns the last accepted command along the requested sub command chain. This command is then used to parse the arguments. This will for sure fail, if the traversing was aborted because an invalid sub command was given. As a result, cobra complains about invalid flags instead of an invalid sub command.\r\n\r\nThis behaviour might be useful, if the intermediate command is *Runnable()*, but it for sure makes no sense, if it isn't.\r\n\r\nThis PR fixes this by providing a *legacyArgs()* error in case of not runnable intermediate commands.\r\n\r\n---\r\n*Remark:* It solves the obvious problematic behaviour, but basically the general scenario is more complex.\r\nIf the intermediate command is *Runnable()* in addition to providing additional sub commands, then it should be possible to forward the control about the error message to the command to be a able to distinguish between these two cases according to its needs. This is basically already possible by declaring a *FlagErrorFunc()*. But unfortunately it only gets the command and error as arguments, but not the actual set of arguments. Therefore it has no chance to detect the actual problem and provide appropriate error feedback.\r\n\r\nSolving this is more invasive, because it would require, either to change the interface, or add another more general error handler option.\r\n\r\n", 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'mandelsoft', 'id': 553075, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'MDQ6VXNlcjU1MzA3NQ==',
