'title': 'fix: treat lone dash as positional during command discovery', 'body': 'When a runnable root command accepts positional arguments and has a `child` subcommand, `root - child` currently executes `child` with `-` as its argument. Replacing `-` with an ordinary filename keeps execution on the root. Enabling `TraverseChildren` also keeps the lone dash on the root, consistent with pflag treating `-` as a positional argument.\n\nUse the existing `isFlagArg` predicate in command discovery and matched-command removal. A lone dash can then stop subcommand discovery like other positional arguments. If an application explicitly defines `-` as a command name or alias, its command token is removed normally. Flag values and the `--` terminator retain their existing handling.\n\nValidation on macOS arm64 with Go 1.25.3:\n\n- The strip-flags case and default-dispatch regressions failed before the fix.\n- Added coverage for lone dashes before and after a subcommand, after a boolean flag, as a flag value, around `--`, and as a command name or alias.\n- `go test ./...` passes.\n- `make all` (formatting and full tests) and `git diff --check` pass. The optional golangci-lint binary is not installed locally.\n\nAI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped implement and test this change.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'ibrahimypr', 'state': 'closed', 'locked': False, 'title': 'fix: prevent completions from mutating os.Args via append side effect', 'body': '## Summary\n\n- Fixes a bug where `getCompletions()` accidentally mutates `os.Args` by writing `"--"` into the shared backing array via an `append` with spare capacity\n- Uses a three-index slice expression (`finalArgs[:len:len]`) to cap the slice capacity, forcing `append` to allocate a new array\n- Adds a regression test that confirms the args slice is not corrupted during shell completion\n\n## Details\n\nWhen shell completions are requested (e.g., `prog __complete x`), `getCompletions()` calls:\n\n```go\n_ = finalCmd.ParseFlags(append(finalArgs, "--"))\n```\n\n`finalArgs` is a sub-slice of the original args (derived from `os.Args[1:]`), and if it has spare capacity in its backing array, `append` writes `"--"` directly into the shared memory rather than allocating a new slice. This corrupts `os.Args`, which users may be inspecting in their `ValidArgsFunction`.\n\nThe fix uses `finalArgs[:len(finalArgs):len(finalArgs)]` to limit the capacity to the length, guaranteeing that `append` allocates a fresh backing array.\n\nThe bug is most visible with `TraverseChildren: true`, since `Traverse()` returns sub-slices that preserve the original backing array\'s capacity.\n\nFixes #2257\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] Added `TestCompletionDoesNotMutateArgs` that fails without the fix and passes with it\n- [x] Full test suite passes (`go test ./...`)', 'author_association': 'title': "command: stop Traverse at `--` so a positional isn't run as a subcommand", 'body': '## Bug (fixes #2528)\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, the long-flag branch of `Command.Traverse` matched a bare `--` as a flag that "takes a value":\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--") && !strings.Contains(arg, "="):\n    inFlag = !hasNoOptDefVal(arg[2:], c.Flags())\n    flags = append(flags, arg)\n    continue\n```\n\n`arg[2:]` is `""`, no flag by that name exists, so `inFlag = true`. The next positional is consumed as that flag\'s "value" and the following positional happens to match a subcommand — so the child handler runs, the first post-`--` positional is silently dropped, and the parent\'s positionals never reach any command.\n\nReproduction from the issue:\n\n```go\nroot := &cobra.Command{Use:"app", TraverseChildren:true, Args:cobra.ArbitraryArgs,\n    Run: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string){ fmt.Printf("root called with %q\\\\n", args) }}\nroot.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{Use:"child",\n    Run: func(*cobra.Command, []string){ fmt.Println("child called") }})\nroot.Execute()\n```\n\n```\n$ ./app -- literal child\nchild called                 # bug: wrong handler, "literal" lost\n$ # expected:\nroot called with ["literal" "child"]\n```\n\nThe default (non-traverse) `stripFlags` path already stops command discovery on `--`.\n\n## Fix\n\nMirror that behaviour. When `Traverse` sees a bare `--`:\n\n1. Parse any flags accumulated so far on the current command.\n2. Return the current command along with the remaining args starting at the delimiter, so a downstream parser sees the exact slice it would have gotten without `TraverseChildren`.\n\n## Test\n\n`TestTraverseStopsAtEndOfFlags` covers two cases:\n\n- `[]string{"--", "literal", "child"}` → traversal stays on root, remaining is unchanged.\n- `[]string{"--", "child"}` → traversal stays on root, remaining is unchanged.\n\n`go test ./...` is green.', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'piyush295', 'id': 126451870, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'U_kgDOB4mAng', 'title': 'fix: stop Traverse command discovery at bare --', 'body': '## Description\n\nFixes #2528.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, `Command.Traverse` treated a bare `--` as a long flag with an empty name (`arg[2:] == ""`). Traverse now does the same: when it sees a bare `--` (and is not already collecting a flag value), it returns the current command with the full args for that level so `Execute` parses flags once and keeps later tokens as positionals.\n\n## Checklist\n\n- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).\n- [x] The code has adequate tests for the new feature / bug.\n- [x] Tests pass: `go test -run TestTraverse .`\n\n## Testing\n\n- New: `TestTraverseBareDoubleDashStopsCommandDiscovery` (`-- literal child`, `-- child`, and plain `child` controls).\n- Existing `TestTraverse*` suite passed locally.\n\n## AI assistance\n\nAI tools helped draft the patch, tests, and PR text. 2510, 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': "Handle combined shorthands in Traverse's value-flag detection", 'body': '## `Traverse` mishandles a combined shorthand cluster that ends in a value flag\n\n### Description\n\n`command.go`, in `Traverse`, the "short flag with a space separated value" case:\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n    inFlag = true\n```\n\n`len(arg) == 2` recognises only a **single** shorthand. A combined cluster such as `-ab` (where `-a` is a bool and `-b` takes a value) is mis-handled: `Traverse` appends `-ab` to `flags` **without** setting `inFlag`, so the following argument is looked up as a **subcommand name**.\n\n### Why it\'s wrong\n\npflag\'s real rule — verified directly with `pflag parse [-ab sub2] err=<nil> args=[] all=true bind="sub2"` — is that the first shorthand lacking a `NoOptDefVal` swallows the rest of the cluster, and only reaches into the next argv slot when it is the *last* shorthand. Cobra must predict that split in order to locate the target command, and for clusters it predicts wrong.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, `prog child -ab grandchild` fails with:\n\n```\nflag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n```\n\neven though the value *was* supplied — and the equivalent `prog child -a -b grandchild` works. Valid input is rejected with a misleading error.\n\n### Upstream status\n\n- Issue **#2188** ("Combining shorthand flags before command names does not work") is open but is about flags *before* the command name (`mycli -C elephant first second`).\n- PR **#2189** ("Fix shorthand combination edge case") is open and unmerged, and its diff touches only `stripFlags` / `argsMinusFirstX` / `Find` — it does **not** touch `Traverse`, so the `TraverseChildren: true` path is unfixed by any open PR.\n\n## The fix\n\n```go\n// shortCombinationTakesNextArg reports whether the value of a single dash\n// shorthand argument (such as "-a" or "-ab") is taken from the following\n// argument, rather than being embedded in the argument itself.\n//\n// This mirrors how pflag parses shorthand arguments: the first shorthand of the\n// combination that does not have a NoOptDefVal consumes the remainder of the\n// combination as its value, and it only reaches out to the next argument when\n// that shorthand is the last one of the combination. So "-ab value" consumes\n// "value" for -b (when -a is a boolean), while "-bvalue" does not.\nfunc shortCombinationTakesNextArg(combination string, fs *flag.FlagSet) bool {\n\tlast := len(combination) - 1\n\tfor i := 0; i <= last; i++ {\n\t\tif !shortHasNoOptDefVal(combination[i:i+1], fs) {\n\t\t\t// This shorthand needs a value. It only comes from the next argument\n\t\t\t// if the combination ends here.\n\t\t\treturn i == last\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n```\n\nand in `Traverse`:\n\n```diff\n-\t\tcase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n+\t\tcase len(arg) > 1 && strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") &&\n+\t\t\tshortCombinationTakesNextArg(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n```\n\nThe `len(arg) > 1` guard is load-bearing: without it a bare `-` (which pflag treats as a positional argument) would start matching and get appended to `flags`.\n\n## Tests\n\n`TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue` (6 subtests) and `TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue`, both added to `command_test.go`.\n\n- Before:\n  ```\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_a_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_an_inherited_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'C\' in -C\n  --- FAIL: TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue\n      command_test.go:2543: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  ```\n  After: all pass.\n- Four control subtests (`value_inside_the_cluster`, `all_boolean_cluster`, `single_value_flag`, `single_bool_flag`) pass **both** before and after, proving the fix does not over-consume arguments.\n- `go test ./...`: root package **404 → 412 PASS** (+8), `cobra/doc` 19 PASS, **0 failures**. Baseline on unmodified HEAD was fully green with zero pre-existing failures. `go vet ./...` clean.\n\nThe 36 `gofmt -l` hits are a pre-existing repo-wide CRLF artefact of this Windows checkout — identical count before and after, so this change adds none.\n\n## Note\n\nThis repository asks contributors to sign a CLA; I have not done so, since that is a legal attestation only the contributor can make.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'januththedev', 'id': 96273863, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'U_kgDOBb0Fxw', 'avatar_url': 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': 'Provide usefull errors when using invalid sub command', 'body': "If the *TraverseChildren* mode is active, the *Traverse* function returns the last accepted command along the requested sub command chain. This command is then used to parse the arguments. This will for sure fail, if the traversing was aborted because an invalid sub command was given. As a result, cobra complains about invalid flags instead of an invalid sub command.\r\n\r\nThis behaviour might be useful, if the intermediate command is *Runnable()*, but it for sure makes no sense, if it isn't.\r\n\r\nThis PR fixes this by providing a *legacyArgs()* error in case of not runnable intermediate commands.\r\n\r\n---\r\n*Remark:* It solves the obvious problematic behaviour, but basically the general scenario is more complex.\r\nIf the intermediate command is *Runnable()* in addition to providing additional sub commands, then it should be possible to forward the control about the error message to the command to be a able to distinguish between these two cases according to its needs. This is basically already possible by declaring a *FlagErrorFunc()*. But unfortunately it only gets the command and error as arguments, but not the actual set of arguments. Therefore it has no chance to detect the actual problem and provide appropriate error feedback.\r\n\r\nSolving this is more invasive, because it would require, either to change the interface, or add 'title': 'fix: treat lone dash as positional during command discovery', 'body': 'When a runnable root command accepts positional arguments and has a `child` subcommand, `root - child` currently executes `child` with `-` as its argument. Replacing `-` with an ordinary filename keeps execution on the root. Enabling `TraverseChildren` also keeps the lone dash on the root, consistent with pflag treating `-` as a positional argument.\n\nUse the existing `isFlagArg` predicate in command discovery and matched-command removal. A lone dash can then stop subcommand discovery like other positional arguments. If an application explicitly defines `-` as a command name or alias, its command token is removed normally. Flag values and the `--` terminator retain their existing handling.\n\nValidation on macOS arm64 with Go 1.25.3:\n\n- The strip-flags case and default-dispatch regressions failed before the fix.\n- Added coverage for lone dashes before and after a subcommand, after a boolean flag, as a flag value, around `--`, and as a command name or alias.\n- `go test ./...` passes.\n- `make all` (formatting and full tests) and `git diff --check` pass. The optional golangci-lint binary is not installed locally.\n\nAI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped implement and test this change.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'ibrahimypr', 'state': 'closed', 'locked': False, 'title': 'fix: prevent completions from mutating os.Args via append side effect', 'body': '## Summary\n\n- Fixes a bug where `getCompletions()` accidentally mutates `os.Args` by writing `"--"` into the shared backing array via an `append` with spare capacity\n- Uses a three-index slice expression (`finalArgs[:len:len]`) to cap the slice capacity, forcing `append` to allocate a new array\n- Adds a regression test that confirms the args slice is not corrupted during shell completion\n\n## Details\n\nWhen shell completions are requested (e.g., `prog __complete x`), `getCompletions()` calls:\n\n```go\n_ = finalCmd.ParseFlags(append(finalArgs, "--"))\n```\n\n`finalArgs` is a sub-slice of the original args (derived from `os.Args[1:]`), and if it has spare capacity in its backing array, `append` writes `"--"` directly into the shared memory rather than allocating a new slice. This corrupts `os.Args`, which users may be inspecting in their `ValidArgsFunction`.\n\nThe fix uses `finalArgs[:len(finalArgs):len(finalArgs)]` to limit the capacity to the length, guaranteeing that `append` allocates a fresh backing array.\n\nThe bug is most visible with `TraverseChildren: true`, since `Traverse()` returns sub-slices that preserve the original backing array\'s capacity.\n\nFixes #2257\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] Added `TestCompletionDoesNotMutateArgs` that fails without the fix and passes with it\n- [x] Full test suite passes (`go test ./...`)', 'author_association': When `Traverse` sees a bare `--`:\n\n1. Parse any flags accumulated so far on the current command.\n2. 'title': 'fix: stop Traverse command discovery at bare --', 'body': '## Description\n\nFixes #2528.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, `Command.Traverse` treated a bare `--` as a long flag with an empty name (`arg[2:] == ""`). The next token was consumed as that flag\'s value, then command discovery resumed, so `./app -- literal child` could execute `child` and drop `literal`.\n\n`stripFlags` / `Find` already stop at `--`. Traverse now does the same: when it sees a bare `--` (and is not already collecting a flag value), it returns the current command with the full args for that level so `Execute` parses flags once and keeps later tokens as positionals.\n\n## Checklist\n\n- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).\n- [x] The code has adequate tests for the new feature / bug.\n- [x] Tests pass: `go test -run TestTraverse .`\n\n## Testing\n\n- New: `TestTraverseBareDoubleDashStopsCommandDiscovery` (`-- literal child`, `-- child`, and plain `child` controls).\n- Existing `TestTraverse*` suite passed locally.\n\n## AI assistance\n\nAI tools helped draft the patch, tests, and PR text. I reviewed the change, ran the tests above, and take responsibility for the contents.', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'ump45nose', 'id': 52391318, 'user_view_type': 'public', 2510, 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': "Handle combined shorthands in Traverse's value-flag detection", 'body': '## `Traverse` mishandles a combined shorthand cluster that ends in a value flag\n\n### Description\n\n`command.go`, in `Traverse`, the "short flag with a space separated value" case:\n\n```go\ncase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n    inFlag = true\n```\n\n`len(arg) == 2` recognises only a **single** shorthand. A combined cluster such as `-ab` (where `-a` is a bool and `-b` takes a value) is mis-handled: `Traverse` appends `-ab` to `flags` **without** setting `inFlag`, so the following argument is looked up as a **subcommand name**.\n\n### Why it\'s wrong\n\npflag\'s real rule — verified directly with `pflag parse [-ab sub2] err=<nil> args=[] all=true bind="sub2"` — is that the first shorthand lacking a `NoOptDefVal` swallows the rest of the cluster, and only reaches into the next argv slot when it is the *last* shorthand. Cobra must predict that split in order to locate the target command, and for clusters it predicts wrong.\n\nWith `TraverseChildren: true`, `prog child -ab grandchild` fails with:\n\n```\nflag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n```\n\neven though the value *was* supplied — and the equivalent `prog child -a -b grandchild` works. Valid input is rejected with a misleading error.\n\n### Upstream status\n\n- Issue **#2188** ("Combining shorthand flags before command names does not work") is open but is about flags *before* the command name (`mycli -C elephant first second`).\n- PR **#2189** ("Fix shorthand combination edge case") is open and unmerged, and its diff touches only `stripFlags` / `argsMinusFirstX` / `Find` — it does **not** touch `Traverse`, so the `TraverseChildren: true` path is unfixed by any open PR.\n\n## The fix\n\n```go\n// shortCombinationTakesNextArg reports whether the value of a single dash\n// shorthand argument (such as "-a" or "-ab") is taken from the following\n// argument, rather than being embedded in the argument itself.\n//\n// This mirrors how pflag parses shorthand arguments: the first shorthand of the\n// combination that does not have a NoOptDefVal consumes the remainder of the\n// combination as its value, and it only reaches out to the next argument when\n// that shorthand is the last one of the combination. So "-ab value" consumes\n// "value" for -b (when -a is a boolean), while "-bvalue" does not.\nfunc shortCombinationTakesNextArg(combination string, fs *flag.FlagSet) bool {\n\tlast := len(combination) - 1\n\tfor i := 0; i <= last; i++ {\n\t\tif !shortHasNoOptDefVal(combination[i:i+1], fs) {\n\t\t\t// This shorthand needs a value. It only comes from the next argument\n\t\t\t// if the combination ends here.\n\t\t\treturn i == last\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n```\n\nand in `Traverse`:\n\n```diff\n-\t\tcase strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") && len(arg) == 2 && !shortHasNoOptDefVal(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n+\t\tcase len(arg) > 1 && strings.HasPrefix(arg, "-") && !strings.Contains(arg, "=") &&\n+\t\t\tshortCombinationTakesNextArg(arg[1:], c.Flags()):\n```\n\nThe `len(arg) > 1` guard is load-bearing: without it a bare `-` (which pflag treats as a positional argument) would start matching and get appended to `flags`.\n\n## Tests\n\n`TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue` (6 subtests) and `TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue`, both added to `command_test.go`.\n\n- Before:\n  ```\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_a_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  --- FAIL: TestTraverseCombinedShorthandWithValue/cluster_ending_in_an_inherited_value_flag\n      command_test.go:2501: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'C\' in -C\n  --- FAIL: TestExecuteCombinedShorthandWithValue\n      command_test.go:2543: Unexpected error: flag needs an argument: \'b\' in -b\n  ```\n  After: all pass.\n- Four control subtests (`value_inside_the_cluster`, `all_boolean_cluster`, `single_value_flag`, `single_bool_flag`) pass **both** before and after, proving the fix does not over-consume arguments.\n- `go test ./...`: root package **404 → 412 PASS** (+8), `cobra/doc` 19 PASS, **0 failures**. Baseline on unmodified HEAD was fully green with zero pre-existing failures. `go vet ./...` clean.\n\nThe 36 `gofmt -l` hits are a pre-existing repo-wide CRLF artefact of this Windows checkout — identical count before and after, so this change adds none.\n\n## Note\n\nThis repository asks contributors to sign a CLA; I have not done so, since that is a legal attestation only the contributor can make.\n', 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'januththedev', 'id': 96273863, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'U_kgDOBb0Fxw', 'avatar_url': 'state': 'open', 'locked': False, 'title': 'Provide usefull errors when using invalid sub command', 'body': "If the *TraverseChildren* mode is active, the *Traverse* function returns the last accepted command along the requested sub command chain. This command is then used to parse the arguments. This will for sure fail, if the traversing was aborted because an invalid sub command was given. As a result, cobra complains about invalid flags instead of an invalid sub command.\r\n\r\nThis behaviour might be useful, if the intermediate command is *Runnable()*, but it for sure makes no sense, if it isn't.\r\n\r\nThis PR fixes this by providing a *legacyArgs()* error in case of not runnable intermediate commands.\r\n\r\n---\r\n*Remark:* It solves the obvious problematic behaviour, but basically the general scenario is more complex.\r\nIf the intermediate command is *Runnable()* in addition to providing additional sub commands, then it should be possible to forward the control about the error message to the command to be a able to distinguish between these two cases according to its needs. This is basically already possible by declaring a *FlagErrorFunc()*. But unfortunately it only gets the command and error as arguments, but not the actual set of arguments. Therefore it has no chance to detect the actual problem and provide appropriate error feedback.\r\n\r\nSolving this is more invasive, because it would require, either to change the interface, or add another more general error handler option.\r\n\r\n", 'author_association': 'NONE', 'user': {'login': 'mandelsoft', 'id': 553075, 'user_view_type': 'public', 'node_id': 'MDQ6VXNlcjU1MzA3NQ==', 'title': 'fix: treat lone dash as positional during command discovery', 'body': 'When a runnable root command accepts positional arguments and has a `child` subcommand, `root - child` currently executes `child` with `-` as its argument. Replacing `-` with an ordinary filename keeps execution on the root. Enabling `TraverseChildren` also keeps the lone dash on the root, consistent with pflag treating `-` as a positional argument.\n\nUse the existing `isFlagArg` predicate in command discovery and matched-command removal. A lone dash can then stop subcommand discovery like other positional arguments. If an application explicitly defines `-` as a command name or alias, its command token is removed normally. 'state': 'closed', 'locked': False, 'title': 'fix: prevent completions from mutating os.Args via append side effect', 'body': '## Summary\n\n- Fixes a bug where `getCompletions()` accidentally mutates `os.Args` by writing `"--"` into the shared backing array via an `append` with spare capacity\n- Uses a three-index slice expression (`finalArgs[:len:len]`) to cap the slice capacity, forcing `append` to allocate a new array\n- Adds a regression test that confirms the args slice is not corrupted during shell completion\n\n## Details\n\nWhen shell completions are requested (e.g., `prog __complete x`), `getCompletions()` calls:\n\n```go\n_ = finalCmd.ParseFlags(append(finalArgs, "--"))\n```\n\n`finalArgs` is a sub-slice of the original args (derived from `os.Args[1:]`), and if it has spare capacity in its backing array, `append` writes `"--"` directly into the shared memory rather than allocating a new slice. This corrupts `os.Args`, which users may be inspecting in their `ValidArgsFunction`.\n\nThe fix uses `finalArgs[:len(finalArgs):len(finalArgs)]` to limit the capacity to the length, guaranteeing that `append` allocates a fresh backing array.\n\nThe bug is most visible with `TraverseChildren: true`, since `Traverse()` returns sub-slices that preserve the original backing array\'s capacity.\n\nFixes #2257\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] Added `TestCompletionDoesNotMutateArgs` that fails without the fix and passes with it\n- [x] Full test suite passes (`go test ./...`)', 'author_association': ### Commit Message
> **Bump pflag to 1.0.8 (#2303)**
>
> In pflag, we recently made a breaking change in naming to be more inclusive. This change, while doing nothing to address the same uninclusive naming in cobra itself, adjusts to those changes to ensure automatic bumps (if you do them) can continue uninterrupted.

### Files Changed (5 additions, 5 deletions)
| File | Changes |
|---|---|
| `command.go` | 2 additions, 2 deletions — Renamed `ParseErrorsWhitelist` → `ParseErrorsAllowlist` from the `flag` package |
| `go.mod` | Updated `spf13/pflag` dependency from `v1.0.6` → `v1.0.8` |
| `go.sum` | Updated checksums for the new pflag version |

---

In short, v1.10.0 is a small maintenance release that bumps the `spf13/pflag` dependency to v1.0.8 to accommodate inclusive naming changes (`Whitelist` → `Allowlist`) in the pflag library.

{'tag_name': 'v2.1.0', 'target_commitish': 'main', 'name': 'v2.1.0', 'body': '# Hello OSC 7501\r\n\r\nThe exciting news in this release is support for the brand new [Program Status Protocol](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status), otherwise known as `OSC 7501`, released just a few days ago. The protocol is designed to allow terminal applications to report what they\'re doing (e.g. idle, working, waiting on the user, finished, or failed) and why.\r\n\r\nThe obvious case for the design is AI agents, but are lots of other use cases for this, and we’re excited to see what you build with it.\r\n\r\nIt’s subtle, but here’s [Crush](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush) in Superlogical’s [Rex](https://www.superlogical.com/updates/public-testing-beginning) with the feature integrated (notice the dot in the first tab).\r\n\r\n<p><img width="700" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85680681-9397-456b-8283-4eed19635681" /></p>\r\n\r\n## Bugfixes\r\n\r\nAlso, this release brings some very important fixes done by @AdamMagued, @simpleqt and @GreedyC.\r\n\r\nCheers!\r\nCharm 🌞\r\n\r\n## Changelog\r\n### New!\r\n* 41bc6265643a4709ad355581b01e6bb70b2ed8ea: feat: OSC 7501 (#1841) (@andrinoff)\r\n### Fixed\r\n* 96d69d2f7eb182bb311be08fc56ed2c208239aff: fix(tty): fall back to default dimensions when terminal size is 0x0 (#1836) (@AdamMagued)\r\n* ff51ba4c51f85875761b15a64f9ab9aa0eaa9fa1: fix: prevent signal goroutine deadlock on shutdown (#1806) (@simpleqt)\r\n### Docs\r\n* 33f6a40ec035111bc11d5fd5304cac1359af44e0: docs: fix command and environment godoc examples (#1833) (@GreedyC)\r\n### Other stuff\r\n* f9df43c4f2c021d8740a2628d59cd810a862eb98: v2.1.0 (@andrinoff)\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n<a href="https://charm.land/"><img alt="The Charm logo" src="https://stuff.charm.sh/charm-banner-next.jpg" width="400"></a>\r\n\r\nThoughts?
